name: theme-shortcuts
description: Box theming: writes one .desktop launcher from $SHORTCUT_NAME/$SHORTCUT_EXEC vars (Desktop + .local/share/applications + /etc/skel), marked trusted for the desktop user so double-click never shows the "Untrusted application launcher" dialog. Reference multiple times with different vars for multiple shortcuts. No attachment. Auto-created idempotently by boxbuilder/vulndb.py.
script:
#!/bin/sh
# theme-shortcuts -- writes one .desktop launcher (Desktop + .local/share/applications
# + /etc/skel) per invocation, reading $SHORTCUT_NAME/$SHORTCUT_EXEC. Multiple
# shortcuts are multiple depends_on/configurations entries against this same
# configuration name with different vars -- nakon's resolve() dedups by (name, vars),
# so each distinct pair runs once as its own step.
set -e

if [ -z "$SHORTCUT_NAME" ] || [ -z "$SHORTCUT_EXEC" ]; then
    echo "[theme-shortcuts] SHORTCUT_NAME/SHORTCUT_EXEC not set; nothing to do" >&2
    exit 0
fi

fname="nakon-theme-$(printf '%s' "$SHORTCUT_NAME" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_').desktop"

nakon_write_shortcut() {
    home="$1"
    desktop="$home/Desktop"
    apps="$home/.local/share/applications"
    mkdir -p "$desktop" "$apps"
    for target in "$desktop" "$apps"; do
        {
            echo '[Desktop Entry]'
            echo 'Type=Application'
            printf 'Name=%s\n' "$SHORTCUT_NAME"
            printf 'Exec=%s\n' "$SHORTCUT_EXEC"
            echo 'Terminal=false'
            echo 'Icon=utilities-terminal'
        } > "$target/$fname"
        chmod 755 "$target/$fname"
    done
}

# gio's metadata::trusted flag is stored PER-USER (gvfs-metadata), so it must be
# set as the desktop user: a root-set flag lands in root's own store and the
# player's desktop still greets every double-click with the "Untrusted
# application launcher" dialog. dbus-launch gives gio a session bus even with no
# X session up yet (metadata lives in ~/.gvfs-metadata, not in X); the short
# sleep lets gvfsd-metadata settle before dbus-launch tears the bus down.
# Best-effort: GNOME/Nautilus 3.38+ and recent xfdesktop are the only
# consumers; everywhere else this is a harmless no-op.
nakon_trust() {
    user="$1"
    home="$2"
    command -v gio >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    if command -v runuser >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        runuser -u "$user" -- dbus-launch \
            gio set "$home/Desktop/$fname" metadata::trusted true 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        su -s /bin/sh "$user" -c \
            "dbus-launch gio set '$home/Desktop/$fname' metadata::trusted true" \
            2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    sleep 1
}

awk -F: '($3>=1000 && $3<60000 && $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/) {print $1":"$6}' /etc/passwd |
while IFS=: read -r nakon_u nakon_h; do
    [ -d "$nakon_h" ] || continue
    nakon_write_shortcut "$nakon_h"
    chown -R "$nakon_u":"$nakon_u" "$nakon_h/Desktop" "$nakon_h/.local/share/applications" \
        2>/dev/null || true
    nakon_trust "$nakon_u" "$nakon_h"
done

# Future users: seed /etc/skel too (root:root -- useradd -m fixes ownership on
# copy). No trust flag here: gvfs metadata is per-user and cannot be pre-seeded
# via skel; team accounts exist at plant time and are handled above.
nakon_write_shortcut /etc/skel

exit 0
